correctness.rationale: In the stated parity basis, H has couplings A=2Jcos(φ/4), B=2Jsin(φ/4), and w=(1,0,1,0)/√2 and v=(1,0,−1,0)/√2 are the sink and source. The real part of a no-jump eigenvalue is −κ|w*ψ|²/(2||ψ||²); equality requires an H-eigenvector orthogonal to w. At generic flux the four H-eigenvalues are distinct and every eigenvector overlaps w, so survival decays. At exact zero flux the decoupled odd mode has no source overlap; the directed reachable three-dimensional restriction has simple H-eigenvalues, all with nonzero sink overlap. The 2π representative is identical by gauge, or by exchanging the parity blocks. At π the Hamiltonian leaves the antisymmetric pair invariant and entirely perpendicular to w, so the prepared state never decays. Independently solving the backward Lyapunov equation K*Q+QK=−I in real coordinates on the stable subspaces gave v*Qv=4/κ+κ(A²+B²)/(A²−B²)² and 3/κ+κ/A² for B=0. The residues therefore differ by 1/κ at fixed κ as φ→0, with no finite-time survival discontinuity. Minimizing c/κ+dκ gives a unique κ=√(c/d), mean 2√(cd); inserting the two coefficients and cos(φ/2)∼−(φ−π)/2 gives all stated optimizer and half-flux scalings.
